title: User guide 5: Built-in science pictures
bullets: Real diagrams of what is being taught, drawn for you
They build up as the narrator speaks
Refraction, photosynthesis, the water cycle, a leaf
subtitle: User guide 5: Built-in science pictures
narration: Welcome to user guide five. Slides can now show the actual thing being taught, as an animated picture. The picture is drawn for you, with labels in the lesson language, and its parts appear exactly as the narrator mentions them.

subtitle: Refraction: the picture builds as it is explained
narration: This is a real frame sequence from a finished video, on refraction of light. First the two media appear, then the normal, then the incident ray, then the refracted ray, and last the two angles. The angles are calculated from the physics, so the ray really bends towards the normal when light enters glass, and away from it when light leaves water.

subtitle: Photosynthesis: sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, chlorophyll, oxygen, glucose
narration: The photosynthesis picture shows sunlight reaching the leaf, water rising from the roots, carbon dioxide entering, the leaf turning bright green when chlorophyll is mentioned, oxygen leaving, and glucose being made. Each part appears when the narrator says it.

subtitle: The water cycle in five stages
narration: The water cycle picture shows the sun heating the sea, water vapour rising, a cloud forming, rain falling on the mountain, and the water flowing back to the sea.

subtitle: Inside a leaf: layers, stomata, chloroplasts
narration: The leaf picture builds up a cross section, layer by layer, then opens the stoma to show gases moving in and out, and finally highlights a chloroplast.

title: How to use them
bullets: The ChatGPT prompt already knows these pictures
Use a picture only when the slide teaches exactly that topic
Write one sentence for each part, in the order the parts appear
You can change a label in the lesson plan if you need other wording
More pictures will be added topic by topic
subtitle: How to use them
narration: You don't have to do anything special, because the prompt in the app already knows these pictures. Use one only when the slide teaches exactly that topic, and write one sentence for each part, in the order the parts appear. Labels can be changed in the lesson plan. More pictures will be added topic by topic. If a topic you need is missing, ask for it to be added.
